subject: Dedicated reservation options and ramping scenarios for BridgePath
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Mills <andrew.mills@bridgepath.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro — Dedicated reservation options and next steps

Hi Andrew,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the clarity on BridgePath's production timeline and the need to lock a predictable GPU footprint before your Q3 launch. As promised, attaching a concise options sheet that lays out three reservation approaches and the expected activation cadence.

Quick summary in the attachment:
- Option A — Anchored Minimum: 24 GPUs reserved (steady-state), 3-month onboarding window.
- Option B — Staged Ramp: Start 12 GPUs, auto-step to 24 at month 4, full 48 by month 10. Includes pre-warm credits.
- Option C — Burst-Ready Slate: 12 guaranteed + 36 burst capacity on soft-commit (pay-for-usage above guaranteed).

Would love your feedback on which path fits procurement and engineering comfort. If helpful, Karthik can draft the activation timeline that lines up with your release milestones.

Attached: 2028-04-25_bridgepath_reservation_options.pdf, draft SOW stub.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Andrew Mills <andrew.mills@bridgepath.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — Dedicated reservation options and next steps

Thanks, Stephanie — useful framing. A couple quick items from procurement/eng after internal sync: 

1) BridgePath prefers a model that keeps near-term spend low while giving capacity certainty by end of Q3. A staged ramp (Option B) looks attractive but we need minimums on each step and a rollback protection if demand doesn't materialize.
2) We must confirm whether burst capacity affects SLAs or whether it's purely soft. Procurement will want explicit failure/fallback behaviors.
3) Our security/compliance team will request SOC2 evidence and a short note on network isolation for the Dedicated environment.

Can you send a variant of the Option B timeline with explicit month-by-month GPU counts, billing treatment (committed vs usage), and the fallback policy (what happens if BridgePath drops below minimums)? Also send any SOC2 and VPC notes we can circulate internally.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Andrew
Andrew Mills
Head of Infrastructure
BridgePath Systems
andrew.mills@bridgepath.io

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Mills <andrew.mills@bridgepath.io>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-26T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — Dedicated reservation options and next steps

Andrew — looping in the detailed ramp variant you asked for. See the proposed activation & billing plan below (month indexes start at contract start = M0). Attached SOW has the same numbers embedded.

--- Proposed Staged Ramp (Option B - explicit variant) ---
M0 (contract execution): 12 reserved GPUs (billing begins at M1) — pre-warm credits: 40 GPU-hours
M1: 12 GPUs (onboarding / testing window)
M2: 12 GPUs
M3: 18 GPUs (apply auto-scale to 18 for peak windows; committed baseline remains 12)
M4: 24 GPUs (committed baseline upgrades to 24)
M5-M7: 24 GPUs
M8: 36 GPUs (optional step-up if utilization >75% for 30 days; customer-triggered or automated by agreement)
M10: 48 GPUs (final committed state if 3-month utilization thresholds met)

Billing notes:
- Committed portion is invoiced monthly at the reserved rate.
- Burst above committed (up to burst capacity) is billed at usage rate; burst does not count toward committed triggers unless customer elects conversion and signs amendment.
- Downgrade/rollback: customer may request a step-down up to one tier (e.g., 48 -> 36) with 60 days notice; immediate reductions are subject to a pro-rated retention fee for the remainder of the billing quarter.

SLA and failure modes:
- Dedicated instances maintain the Redwood 99.9% uptime SLA for committed capacity. Burst capacity is best-effort and not SLA-backed.
- If regional capacity constraints occur, Redwood will route traffic to a compatible model variant in a nearby region (customer opt-in required) or provide temporary rate-limited fallbacks until capacity is restored.

Compliance & network isolation:
- Redwood Private (VPC deployment) option supports single-tenant control plane and customer-managed VPC peering. SOC2 Type II report available; I'll attach the redacted evidence pack.

Attachments referenced: SOW-BridgePath-v1.docx (term sheet embedded), SOC2-evidence-redacted.zip (will share via secure link).

Let us know if you'd like Karthik to convert the above into a single-column activation calendar for procurement.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions & Capacity Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Andrew Mills <andrew.mills@bridgepath.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-27T16:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — Dedicated reservation options and next steps

Appreciate the detail, Karthik. This aligns well with our finance forecast and the 60-day rollback term gives us the guardrail we need. Procurement will review the SOW and I expect a redline by end of next week.

Two small asks before we move to signatures: 
- Please confirm the DocuSign workflow and the list of signatories (we'll need legal + procurement + engineering).
- Can Stephanie send the SOC2 summary and VPC design note to security@bridgepath.io directly? They want to triage any outstanding questions before the redline.

If those two items are ok, I think we're ready to proceed to internal approval.

Thanks — Andrew
